recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the published FHIR-11083 correction in current build-relevant source without changing unrelated client-authentication mechanisms or out-of-build proposal notes.
issue_request: FHIR-11083 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for FHIR-core Security. It asked to replace wording that OAuth may authenticate and/or authorize users with wording that OpenID Connect may authenticate users and OAuth 2.0 (or later) may authorize access.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioned FHIR-11083 or GF#11083. Historical security narrative commit 95ee245e72e4bd1ac09824738ae7b5f7519239ef introduced OpenID Connect authentication wording but retained an OAuth authenticate/authorize sentence, and d417c5d674a4a6b7e4af8d9ef15b7d55d3b4d3e8 later moved that stale sentence into Access Control. The combined branch already contains a separate FHIR-16532 checklist fix that did not fully resolve FHIR-11083's remaining source inconsistencies.
additional_context: source/security.html, source/safety.html, and source/ehr-fm.html are root pages in the current source hierarchy. source/fhir.ini actively lists the safety code system and active CapabilityStatement and MessageHeader resources, so the matching code-system, CapabilityStatement example, and $process-message OperationDefinition edits are in current build scope. Later FHIR-16532 and FHIR-34362 decisions support keeping authentication guidance distinct from OAuth authorization/access-token enforcement. Community searches found no conflicting human discussion.
reconciliation: Published one source-changing commit that removes remaining OAuth-as-authentication language from active current source, specifies OAuth 2.0 (or later) where appropriate, and aligns parallel security/safety/EHR/example/operation text with the FHIR-11083 protocol distinction.
source_changes: source/security.html: specified OAuth 2.0 in the summary and changed the Access Control recommendation from OAuth authenticate/authorize to OAuth 2.0 authorization.
source/safety.html: replaced the web-centric OAuth authentication note with OpenID Connect authentication plus OAuth 2.0 authorization guidance.
source/codesystem/codesystem-safety-entries.xml: aligned the safety checklist code-system definition with OAuth 2.0 profile wording.

source/ehr-fm.html: changed the EHR-FM authentication mapping from OAuth as preferred mechanism to OpenID Connect or another authentication protocol, and clarified OAuth 2.0-based authorization for access control.
source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-phr-example.xml: changed the PHR example from generic OAuth authentication/authorization service wording to OAuth 2.0 authorization service wording.
source/messageheader/operationdefinition-MessageHeader-process-message.xml: changed $process-message mailbox security text from OAuth authentication to OAuth 2.0 bearer token authorization.
